title: Senate Republicans reject effort to halt Iran war, but some eye future war powers votes
byline: The Republican-led Senate on Wednesday rejected the latest Democratic attempt to halt President Donald Trump’s war in Iran, turning aside a resolution that would require the U.S. to withdraw forces from the conflict until Congress authorizes further action.

title: Major fire at Australian oil refinery to impact nation’s petrol supplies
byline: A major fire has broken out at one of Australia’s two oil refineries, deepening fears over the nation’s petrol supplies amid a global fuel crunch.

title: Fairly heavy rainfall expected in parts of the island
byline: The Meteorology Department says showers or thundershowers will occur at several places in Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, Central, Uva and North-western provinces after 1.00 pm.

title: Sri Lanka assures uninterrupted travel for Bangladeshis despite global crisis
byline: Travel to Sri Lanka remains fully unaffected for Bangladeshi tourists despite ongoing global conflicts and economic uncertainties, said Buddhika Hewawasam, Chairman of Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau, while talking to The Bangladesh Monitor during a media networking session held at Le Meridien Dhaka on April 5.

title: Auspicious time for commencing urgent duties falls tomorrow
byline: The auspicious time for departing for urgent duties, as specified in the Sinhala and Tamil New Year auspicious time schedule (‘Nekath Seettuwa’), falls tomorrow (April 17).

title: Chinese FM says reopening of Strait of Hormuz is a “unanimous demand” of international community
byline: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told his Iranian counterpart that reopening the Strait of Hormuz was a unanimous demand from the international community.

title: Trump says talks between leaders of Israel and Lebanon ‘will happen’ on Thursday
byline: US president Donald Trump has said talks between the leaders of Israel and Lebanon “will happen” on Thursday.

title: Legal action initiated against over 400 traders during festive season – PHIs
byline: The Public Health Inspectors’ Union (PHIU) states that legal action has been initiated against more than 400 traders following island-wide inspections conducted in view of the Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

title: Nine Chinese cybercrime suspects arrested at BIA
byline: A total of nine Chinese nationals were arrested at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayaka early this morning (16) while attempting to enter the country to allegedly engage in cybercrime-related activities.

title: Private bus and train services to gradually normalize from today
byline: The Lanka Private Bus Owners’ Association (LPBOA) has announced that steps will be taken to operate between 50% and 60% of the private bus fleet island-wide starting today (16).

title: Police to seize vehicles with non-standard number plates
byline: Sri Lanka Police have announced that vehicles fitted with number plates that do not comply with prescribed standards will be taken into police custody and produced before court.

title: Fishing vessel with suspected narcotics haul intercepted in naval operation
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy has taken into custody a local multi-day fishing vessel carrying several sacks suspected to contain narcotics during a special operation conducted in deep-sea waters south of Sri Lanka.

title: Pope Leo to hold peace meeting in Cameroon amid Trump attacks
byline: Pope Leo was scheduled to travel to the biggest city in Cameroon’s conflict-hit anglophone region on Thursday, the latest stop on an ambitious four-country Africa tour amid attacks on the pontiff by U.S. President Donald Trump.

title: SLTB to introduce card-only payment system for bus fares - chairman
byline: All necessary arrangements have been made to introduce a card-only payment system for Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) bus fares in the near future, says SLTB Chairman Sanjeewa Kanagaratne.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central and Uva provinces and in Galle, Matara and Kurunegala districts.

title: Police to take strict action against vehicles emitting excessive black smoke
byline: Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Traffic Control and Road Safety, W.P.J. Senadheera, said that strict legal action will be taken against vehicles emitting excessive black smoke while operating on public roads.

title: Sri Lanka better positioned to support vulnerable amid energy risks – IMF
byline: Sri Lanka has strengthened its fiscal position over the past three years, placing it in a better position to support vulnerable groups affected by global energy shocks, according to the IMF’s Asia and Pacific Director, Krishna Srinivasan.

title: TIME releases list of ‘100 most influential people’; Trump, Mamdani, Netanyahu among top leaders
byline: TIME released its list of the ‘100 Most Influential People of 2026’ on Wednesday, naming Pope Leo, US President Donald Trump, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, among others.

title: Six Chinese nationals arrested with smuggled cigarettes at BIA
byline: A total of six Chinese nationals who illegally brought a consignment of cigarettes into the country have been arrested by Customs officers at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA).

title: Two dead, six missing in drowning incident at Deduru Oya - Police
byline: Two bodies have been recovered, while two others have been hospitalized and six individuals reportedly remain missing after a group of 15 went bathing in the Deduru Oya near the Kuratiyagahamula area of Nikaweratiya within the Kobeigane Police Division, police said.

title: First crude oil tanker since Middle East conflict to arrive in Sri Lanka tomorrow
byline: Ceylon Petroleum Storage Terminals Limited (CPSTL) has announced that the first crude oil tanker to arrive since the onset of the Middle East conflict is scheduled to reach the island tomorrow (17).

title: Israeli strike severs last bridge linking southern Lebanon to rest of country – report
byline: An Israeli strike has severed the last bridge linking southern ⁠Lebanon to the rest of the country, a senior Lebanese security official told ⁠Reuters, adding that the strike “shattered” the ⁠bridge and left no ⁠possibility of repairing ⁠it.

title: 44 dead in 42 road accidents reported during festive period: Police
byline: Sri Lanka Police reported a total of 42 road traffic accidents across the island between April 10 and 15, resulting in 44 fatalities.

title: Registration of Persons Dept. temporarily suspends services tomorrow due to system failure
byline: The Department for Registration of Persons (ID Office) has announced that all public services, including the one-day service at its head office and all provincial offices, will be suspended tomorrow (April 17).

title: Fuel and electricity supply to continue uninterrupted despite Middle East conflict – Minister
byline: Minister of Health and Mass Media, Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa, has stated that Sri Lanka’s fuel and electricity supply will continue without interruption despite the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

title: Pakistan says no dates set for second round of US-Iran talks
byline: No dates have been decided for the second round of talks between ⁠the U.S. and Iran, a spokesperson for Pakistan’s foreign ministry said on Thursday.

title: Warm weather advisory issued for most parts of the country
byline: A warm weather advisory has been issued for residents of the Northern, North-Central, North-Western, Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern, and Eastern provinces and the Monaragala district.

title: Police statement on arrest of ex-MP Chandana Kathriarachchi
byline: Sri Lanka Police has issued a statement regarding the arrest of former Member of Parliament Chandana Kathriarachchi by the Colombo Crimes Division (CCD).

title: Ranbir Kapoor makes history as only Bollywood star on TIME 100 list
byline: In a major global milestone, Ranbir Kapoor has been named among TIME Magazine’s 100 most influential people, becoming the only Bollywood actor to feature on this year’s prestigious list.

title: Further details emerge on arrest of ex-MP Chandana Kathriarachchi
byline: Further details have emerged regarding the arrest of former Member of Parliament Chandana Kathriarachchi by the Colombo Crimes Division (CCD).

title: Google should allow third-party search engines access to data, EU says
byline: The European Commission has proposed that Google allow third-party search engines to access its search data, including that of artificial intelligence chatbots with search functionalities, to comply with the Digital Markets Act, the commission said on Thursday.

title: Former MP Chandana Kathriarachchi arrested
byline: Former Member of Parliament Chandana Kathriarachchi has been arrested by the Colombo Crimes Division (CCD).

title: Europe could run out of jet fuel in 6 weeks, IEA warns
byline: Europe may have just six weeks left of jet fuel, with serious consequences for the continent’s economy, the International Energy Agency warned on Thursday.

title: Israel and Lebanon agree to 10-day ceasefire, Trump says
byline: The leaders of Israel and Lebanon agreed to a 10-day ceasefire after officials from the two countries met in Washington, D.C., President Donald Trump said Thursday.

title: Pope criticises ‘tyrants’ who spend billions on wars after Trump spat
byline: Pope Leo has criticised leaders who spend billions on wars and said the world was “being ravaged by a handful of tyrants” in unusually forceful comments during a visit to Cameroon.

title: Trump says will invite Netanyahu and Lebanese President Aoun to White House
byline: Moments after announcing a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, US President Donald Trump says he will be inviting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Lebanese President Joseph Aoun to the White House “for the first meaningful talks between Israel and Lebanon since 1983.”

title: SriLankan Airlines suspends Country Manager over incident at Bangkok airport
byline: SriLankan Airlines has clarified what it describes as inaccurate and misleading media reports regarding an alleged clash involving an airline official and flight crew at Bangkok’s Suvarnabhumi International Airport.
